bug_semantics: The /api/system/getConf endpoint returns the application configuration via GetMaskedConf() -> HideConfSecret(), but the masking list is incomplete: fields such as the session-cookie signing key (CookieKey), the pandoc binary path (Export.PandocBin, which leaks the OS username via C:\Users\<name>), the encrypted-notebook key material (NotebookCrypto key fields), and workspace paths (System.WorkspaceDir) are not hidden. Anonymous or publish-reader (unprivileged) users can therefore read these secrets, forge/tamper with signed session cookies to impersonate any user, learn OS-username paths, and obtain encrypted-notebook key material; on instances without an access-auth code configured this escalates to administrator (CWE-522 Insufficiently Protected Credentials).
flaw_origin: Commit ba2193403da71a679dcde24e5b6284278b7240da ("Support read-only publish service", 2024-06-12, author Yingyi / 颖逸 <49649786+Zuoqiu-Yingyi@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub) introduced the read-only publish service role that can reach getConf without authentication, together with the first HideConfSecret() implementation in kernel/model/conf.go — a hard-coded masking list (c.AI, c.Api, c.Flashcard, c.LocalIPs, c.Publish, c.Repo, c.Sync, c.System.{AppDir,ConfDir,DataDir,HomeDir,Name,NetworkProxy}) that already omitted CookieKey, Export.PandocBin, NotebookCrypto key material, and System.WorkspaceDir. The incomplete-denylist design at the BIC is the flaw the advisory names: every later disclosure (CookieKey hidden 2026-07-25 77421530, encrypted-notebook keys hidden 2026-07-24 3bc014c7, pandoc/workspace paths hidden 2026-07-25 2d8b9839, lifecycle guard 2026-07-31 37820739) closes one more entry the BIC's list never contained. Parent tree 536879cb has neither the publish service role nor HideConfSecret (introducer_parent_absent=true for the masking function).
